source.title: An Ode to an ODE
source.authors: K. Choromanski; J. Davis; Valerii Likhosherstov; Xing-You Song; J. Slotine; Jacob Varley; Honglak Lee; Adrian Weller; Vikas Sindhwani

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own training and supervised-learning results for Neural ODE architectures, bearing on initialization and normalization-related claim versions, but does not use the benchmark training-error measures specified in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports policy rewards and image test accuracy, not training classification error. It does not report training error results on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100. Table 1 and Table 2 compare test accuracies across corrupted MNIST variants; RL reward curves are presented in Figure 2.
record.test_reason: The study uses orthogonality to stabilize a proposed Neural ODE architecture and reports its task performance. It does not compare initializations for training speed or trainable depth (V4), or test any other version. Maintaining orthogonality throughout training and proving gradient bounds do not establish the initialization effects V4 names.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion. More precisely, they prove gradient bounds for their constrained architecture and conditional convergence guarantees, then report downstream accuracy and reward gains. The experiments do not directly isolate initialization effects or measure vanishing/exploding gradients.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes nested Neural ODEs with an orthogonal matrix parameter-flow; its supervised experiments use corrupted MNIST and report test accuracy, rather than the claim's benchmark training-error measure.
record.method_sensitivity: In the reported corrupted-MNIST experiments, dropout rate and hidden width differ between Tables 1 and 2; the paper also reports that HyperNet and DeepNet variants failed to learn on some RL tasks. These conditions are not evidence about the claim's named training-error measure.

fits_no_version.finding: ODEtoODE variants achieve competitive test accuracies across the reported corrupted-MNIST variants.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Nested Neural ODEs with orthogonal parameter flows can improve test classification performance over the tested architecture baselines.

fits_no_version.finding: ODEtoODE is reported as best on four RL tasks and among the two best on the remaining four.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Orthogonal parameter-flow Neural ODE policies trained with evolution strategies perform strongly on the tested control tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: Lemma 4.1 bounds intermediate activation-gradient norms between 1/e and e times the terminal gradient norm on the unit time interval, assuming orthogonal parameter flows and an activation with derivative magnitude one.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The specified continuously constrained Neural ODE architecture has bounded backpropagated activation-gradient norms on a fixed unit time interval.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 1 gives a conditional stationary-point convergence bound for the Gaussian-smoothed RL objective, with constants independent of discretization depth and bounded parameter iterates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the stated assumptions, stochastic Riemannian optimization of ISO-ODEtoODE has a convergence guarantee independent of discretization depth.

record.problems: The supervised results report test accuracy only, with no training-error measurements; uncertainty is not reported for the accuracy tables. RL curves summarize 10 seeds, but plotted reward values are not tabulated in the supplied text. The authors state that no ablation studies were run on ODEtoODEs.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying benchmark training-error results were reported. Figure 2 includes several comparator curves and task-specific reward outcomes, but no exact values are stated in the text; they are not extracted as separate rows because they do not measure training classification error.

untested.parts: Training classification error of convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including random labels and recipe-dependent failures.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training-error degradation with depth in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks, prevention by identity shortcuts, and the specified initialization alternatives.

Activation-matched initialization effects on learning speed and trainable depth; orthogonal versus equal-variance Gaussian initialization; very deep plain tanh and convolutional networks. The study constrains weights throughout training rather than isolating initialization.
Loss recovery, divergence and sharpness dynamics relative to learning-rate stability thresholds.
Batch normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and matched comparisons with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Corrupted MNIST here concerns image corruptions, not random or corrupted training labels. The text's claim of winning 11 of 15 Table 1 tasks is inconsistent with the 11 listed dataset conditions; do not repeat that count as a verified result.

versions.untested_parts: No CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 training classification error, corrupted labels, random labels, or small-model/early-stopping training-error results.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student problem or student-width sweep against teacher size.
No plain-versus-residual depth comparison of training error, nor Fixup or normalization ablation.

The study proposes orthogonal matrix flows and claims gradient stabilization, but its empirical comparisons report task performance rather than training speed or trainable depth under matched initializations.
No learning-rate stability threshold or curvature/sharpness measurements.
No batch-normalization comparison or normalization-based training-speed measurements.

rows.subject: ODEtoODE
rows.operation_detail: Policy rewards on four OpenAI Gym and four DeepMind Control Suite tasks.

conditions.value: Humanoid, HalfCheetah, and six additional tasks shown in Figure 2

rows.value: Authors state ODEtoODE is solely the best performing algorithm on four of eight tasks and one of the two best on the remaining four.
rows.note: Reward-task performance does not measure the training classification error claim. Some exact per-task values are figure-only.
rows.check: The authors' performance summary is accurate, but policy rewards under evolution strategies do not measure any version. This aggregates eight tasks and is a comparison of the study's own method with baselines.
